bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Occupational health and safety exposure in chemical manufacturing — BRSR flags this as both a risk and an opportunity: manufacturing operations involve exposure to operational, chemical and workplace hazards, making health and safety management critical for workforce well-being and operational continuity; mitigation is periodic training, safety audits, risk assessments, preventive controls and a strong safety culture.
- Business ethics and compliance / anti-trust exposure — BRSR identifies non-compliance with business ethics and anti-trust regulations as a risk that may lead to legal, financial and reputational consequences; mitigated through periodic surveys, mandatory training, stronger governance frameworks and adherence to anti-trust and regulatory requirements.
- Single-activity concentration — 100% of turnover comes from one activity - manufacturing and sale of synthetic organic colouring matter (dyes and pigments 74%, prepared pigments and other colouring matter 26%), so the Company has no diversification outside the pigment value chain.
- Export and geographic exposure — Exports contributed 25.87% of total turnover in FY2025-26 and international markets are served via associated entities, leaving a meaningful share of revenue exposed to cross-border trade dynamics and currency movement.
- High and rising employee attrition — Turnover rate for permanent employees rose to 29% in FY2025-26 (male 27%, female 46%) from 20.94% in FY2024-25 and 20% in FY2023-24; permanent worker turnover was much lower at 4.5%.
- Key management transition at the CFO level — Mr. Jugal Sahu resigned as Chief Financial Officer effective close of business hours on March 09, 2026, and Mr. Nilkanth Natu was appointed Interim Chief Financial Officer only after the year end, effective May 11, 2026; no women are represented among Key Management Personnel.
- Concentrated promoter control and reduced public float — After the Open Offer completed on October 03, 2025, the Acquirer along with PAC-1, PAC-2 and PAC-3 exercise control over 70.25% of the total voting share capital, held indirectly by Sudarshan Chemical Industries Limited through Sudarshan Switzerland HLD1 AG (36.56%), Sudarshan Switzerland HLD2 AG (17.80%) and Sudarshan Europe B.V. (15.89%).
- Legacy of the Heubach Group insolvency and post-acquisition integration — Heubach GmbH and Heubach Group GmbH (the erstwhile holding company of a promoter shareholder) filed for insolvency proceedings before the Braunschweig court in 2024; the global pigment business was acquired by Sudarshan Europe B.V. on March 03, 2025 through an interdependent asset-and-share deal, and the Company is now being integrated into the Sudarshan Chemical Group.
- Product quality and logistics complaints from customers — Under the BRSR grievance disclosure, customer complaints closed during FY2025-26 comprised 50 on product quality and 24 on product logistics, indicating service and quality issues are an ongoing operational watch-item.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company manufactures and sells synthetic organic colouring matter - organic and inorganic pigments, pigment preparations, dyes and specialty materials - for paints and coatings, plastics, printing and digital printing, and special applications. It runs a dedicated R&D centre in Navi Mumbai plus application and analytical laboratories across India, with established capabilities in high-value applications such as automotive coatings and digital printing. Through its associated entities the Company exports to more than 75 countries, serves over 100 domestic customers and offers a portfolio of over 500 products.

outlook.body:
- Complete the integration into ONE Sudarshan and operate as an integrated node of the group, drawing on a global platform of 19 manufacturing facilities across 11 countries, 3,825 employees, R&D capabilities and commercial infrastructure
- Sharpen focus on pigments as the core of the business, supported by a broader product portfolio, disciplined cost reduction and improved capacity utilisation across facilities
- Optimize the manufacturing footprint across the Group - select AZO products are being transitioned from Frankfurt to Roha, while Cuddalore is building a combination of commodity and specialty products for the broader industrial market
- Move the portfolio up the value chain toward specialty and high-performance grades, which showed better resilience than commodity pigments
- Position as a full-service colorant partner rather than a single-category supplier, using the broader ONE Sudarshan portfolio to win back and expand accounts
- Direct innovation at recycling-compatible pigments, sustainable color solutions and application-led products through a two-level framework of Life Cycle Innovation (enhancing existing products) and Top Line Innovation (entirely new products for specific segments, applications or regions)
- Localize the premium HP Azo range to unlock new export opportunities from FY2027 onward
- Manage raw material, currency and supply chain volatility through supply chain diversification, strategic inventory positioning and long-term partnerships, aided by ONE Sudarshan procurement leverage
- Treat sustainability as a commercial discipline - raise renewable energy share across sites and prioritise investments that reduce operating costs while advancing environmental commitments
- Decide with a three-year horizon rather than a quarterly one, accepting near-term margin pressure where needed to protect long-term customer relationships
- Strengthen governance and financial oversight, including the appointment of PricewaterhouseCoopers Services LLP as Internal Auditor and transition to a unified reporting framework across the Group
- A comprehensive Double Materiality Assessment (DMA) was undertaken at the Sudarshan Chemical Industries Limited level; its material topics, impacts, risks and opportunities are treated as applicable to Sudarshan Colorants India Limited, which forms the current reporting boundary. BRSR disclosures are made on a standalone basis with no external assessment or assurance provider.
- Climate Change & Energy Source Diversification is identified as an opportunity: transitioning to clean fuels and renewable energy can reduce GHG emissions and operating costs over the long term while strengthening business resilience, supporting decarbonization targets and enhancing competitiveness in global markets.
- Product Stewardship & Innovation is identified as an opportunity: developing sustainable and bio-based alternatives can reduce the environmental footprint of products while supporting evolving customer demand and regulatory expectations.
- Occupational Health & Safety is managed through periodic training, safety audits, risk assessments, preventive controls and promotion of a strong safety culture across operations.
- Employee Development & Engagement is identified as an opportunity to strengthen employer branding and the Employee Value Proposition through skills, workplace culture and talent attraction and retention.
- Business Ethics & Compliance is addressed through periodic surveys, mandatory training programmes, stronger governance frameworks and adherence to anti-trust and regulatory requirements.
- Grievance redressal mechanisms are in place for every stakeholder group - complaint registers at the main entry gate across sites for communities plus a grievance.redressal@sudarshan.com email for communities, employees, workers and customers; shares@sudarshan.com for shareholders; and published investor contact details.
- CSR is applicable to the Company under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013.
- Diversity: women are 11% of total employees and 5% of total workers (permanent workers 1%), and 33% of the Board of Directors, with no female representation among Key Management Personnel.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Under the head 'Capacity Expansion', the Directors' Report states that during the year the Company continued its expansion plans and incurred capex spend of Rs 25.34 Crore; no individual project cost or commissioning schedule is disclosed. The larger expansion story is footprint optimisation within the group: the Company took deliberate steps to optimize the manufacturing footprint across the Group, with select AZO products being transitioned from Frankfurt to Roha, while Cuddalore is building a combination of commodity and specialty products for the broader industrial market. Entering FY2027 the stated operating priority is a broader product portfolio, disciplined cost reduction and improved capacity utilization across the existing facilities at Navi Mumbai, Roha, Cuddalore and Nagda, rather than greenfield addition. Efforts to localize the premium HP Azo range are taking shape and are expected to unlock new export opportunities from FY2027 onward. Footprint also expanded indirectly through the group: Sudarshan Europe B.V. completed the acquisition of the Heubach Group on March 3, 2025, bringing 58 subsidiaries (including step-down subsidiaries) and two joint venture companies into the Sudarshan Chemical Group, giving the Company access to a ONE Sudarshan platform of 19 manufacturing facilities across 11 countries, 3,825 employees and 4,000+ global customers, plus technical centres and application expertise. On the energy side, a solar installation at Roha now meets approximately 50% of that facility's electricity demand and a hybrid wind-solar model at Cuddalore lifted renewable electricity share from approximately 62% to 75%.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The destocking cycle has largely run its course, and domestic demand, particularly in coatings and plastics, is expected to strengthen through FY2027
- Management is targeting a return to growth, supported by new account wins and an expanded portfolio via the ONE Sudarshan group
- FY2026 revenue declined, reflecting global market softness, customer inventory destocking and the natural caution that accompanies a year of organizational transition
- Outside the US, markets grew 7%; an uncertain tariff environment weighed on US export momentum
- Coatings remained the most stable segment, with specialty and high-performance grades showing better resilience than commodity pigments; printing inks were softer on global destocking, expected to ease as inventory positions normalize through FY2027
- Near-term commercial opportunities in India are recycling-compatible pigments, driven by tightening packaging regulations, and low-migration, food-contact compliant grades, where domestic demand is expanding quickly
- Customers who previously sourced certain specialty grades elsewhere have returned, as the broader ONE Sudarshan portfolio opens doors
- Volatility in raw material costs, currency movements and supply chains remains an operating reality
- A largely debt-free balance sheet gives flexibility to prioritize investments that reduce operating costs while advancing environmental commitments
- Demand for pigments is expected to remain supported by resilient end-use industries, although geopolitical uncertainties and evolving trade dynamics may continue to influence supply chains and market sentiment
- Being a full-service colorant partner rather than a single-category supplier is beginning to show up in the FY2027 pipeline, with customers who previously sourced certain specialty grades elsewhere returning to the Company

risks.risk: Occupational health and safety exposure in chemical manufacturing
risks.note: BRSR flags this as both a risk and an opportunity: manufacturing operations involve exposure to operational, chemical and workplace hazards, making health and safety management critical for workforce well-being and operational continuity; mitigation is periodic training, safety audits, risk assessments, preventive controls and a strong safety culture.

risks.risk: Business ethics and compliance / anti-trust exposure
risks.note: BRSR identifies non-compliance with business ethics and anti-trust regulations as a risk that may lead to legal, financial and reputational consequences; mitigated through periodic surveys, mandatory training, stronger governance frameworks and adherence to anti-trust and regulatory requirements.

100% of turnover comes from one activity - manufacturing and sale of synthetic organic colouring matter (dyes and pigments 74%, prepared pigments and other colouring matter 26%), so the Company has no diversification outside the pigment value chain.

Exports contributed 25.87% of total turnover in FY2025-26 and international markets are served via associated entities, leaving a meaningful share of revenue exposed to cross-border trade dynamics and currency movement.
Turnover rate for permanent employees rose to 29% in FY2025-26 (male 27%, female 46%) from 20.94% in FY2024-25 and 20% in FY2023-24; permanent worker turnover was much lower at 4.5%.

risks.risk: Key management transition at the CFO level
risks.note: Mr. Jugal Sahu resigned as Chief Financial Officer effective close of business hours on March 09, 2026, and Mr. Nilkanth Natu was appointed Interim Chief Financial Officer only after the year end, effective May 11, 2026; no women are represented among Key Management Personnel.

risks.risk: Concentrated promoter control and reduced public float
risks.note: After the Open Offer completed on October 03, 2025, the Acquirer along with PAC-1, PAC-2 and PAC-3 exercise control over 70.25% of the total voting share capital, held indirectly by Sudarshan Chemical Industries Limited through Sudarshan Switzerland HLD1 AG (36.56%), Sudarshan Switzerland HLD2 AG (17.80%) and Sudarshan Europe B.V. (15.89%).

risks.risk: Legacy of the Heubach Group insolvency and post-acquisition integration
risks.note: Heubach GmbH and Heubach Group GmbH (the erstwhile holding company of a promoter shareholder) filed for insolvency proceedings before the Braunschweig court in 2024; the global pigment business was acquired by Sudarshan Europe B.V. on March 03, 2025 through an interdependent asset-and-share deal, and the Company is now being integrated into the Sudarshan Chemical Group.

risks.risk: Product quality and logistics complaints from customers
risks.note: Under the BRSR grievance disclosure, customer complaints closed during FY2025-26 comprised 50 on product quality and 24 on product logistics, indicating service and quality issues are an ongoing operational watch-item.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Sudarshan Colorants India Limited (formerly Heubach Colorants India Limited) is among the world's leading producers of organic pigments and is now part of the Sudarshan Chemical Group's 'ONE Sudarshan' platform.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures and sells synthetic organic colouring matter - organic and inorganic pigments, pigment preparations, dyes and specialty materials - for paints and coatings, plastics, printing and digital printing, and special applications. It runs a dedicated R&D centre in Navi Mumbai plus application and analytical laboratories across India, with established capabilities in high-value applications such as automotive coatings and digital printing. Through its associated entities the Company exports to more than 75 countries, serves over 100 domestic customers and offers a portfolio of over 500 products.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The destocking cycle has largely run its course, and domestic demand, particularly in coatings and plastics, is expected to strengthen through FY2027
- Management is targeting a return to growth, supported by new account wins and an expanded portfolio via the ONE Sudarshan group
- FY2026 revenue declined, reflecting global market softness, customer inventory destocking and the natural caution that accompanies a year of organizational transition
- Outside the US, markets grew 7%; an uncertain tariff environment weighed on US export momentum
- Coatings remained the most stable segment, with specialty and high-performance grades showing better resilience than commodity pigments; printing inks were softer on global destocking, expected to ease as inventory positions normalize through FY2027
- Near-term commercial opportunities in India are recycling-compatible pigments, driven by tightening packaging regulations, and low-migration, food-contact compliant grades, where domestic demand is expanding quickly
- Customers who previously sourced certain specialty grades elsewhere have returned, as the broader ONE Sudarshan portfolio opens doors
- Volatility in raw material costs, currency movements and supply chains remains an operating reality
- A largely debt-free balance sheet gives flexibility to prioritize investments that reduce operating costs while advancing environmental commitments
- Demand for pigments is expected to remain supported by resilient end-use industries, although geopolitical uncertainties and evolving trade dynamics may continue to influence supply chains and market sentiment
- Being a full-service colorant partner rather than a single-category supplier is beginning to show up in the FY2027 pipeline, with customers who previously sourced certain specialty grades elsewhere returning to the Company

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Complete the integration into ONE Sudarshan and operate as an integrated node of the group, drawing on a global platform of 19 manufacturing facilities across 11 countries, 3,825 employees, R&D capabilities and commercial infrastructure
- Sharpen focus on pigments as the core of the business, supported by a broader product portfolio, disciplined cost reduction and improved capacity utilisation across facilities
- Optimize the manufacturing footprint across the Group - select AZO products are being transitioned from Frankfurt to Roha, while Cuddalore is building a combination of commodity and specialty products for the broader industrial market
- Move the portfolio up the value chain toward specialty and high-performance grades, which showed better resilience than commodity pigments
- Position as a full-service colorant partner rather than a single-category supplier, using the broader ONE Sudarshan portfolio to win back and expand accounts
- Direct innovation at recycling-compatible pigments, sustainable color solutions and application-led products through a two-level framework of Life Cycle Innovation (enhancing existing products) and Top Line Innovation (entirely new products for specific segments, applications or regions)
- Localize the premium HP Azo range to unlock new export opportunities from FY2027 onward
- Manage raw material, currency and supply chain volatility through supply chain diversification, strategic inventory positioning and long-term partnerships, aided by ONE Sudarshan procurement leverage
- Treat sustainability as a commercial discipline - raise renewable energy share across sites and prioritise investments that reduce operating costs while advancing environmental commitments
- Decide with a three-year horizon rather than a quarterly one, accepting near-term margin pressure where needed to protect long-term customer relationships
- Strengthen governance and financial oversight, including the appointment of PricewaterhouseCoopers Services LLP as Internal Auditor and transition to a unified reporting framework across the Group
- A comprehensive Double Materiality Assessment (DMA) was undertaken at the Sudarshan Chemical Industries Limited level; its material topics, impacts, risks and opportunities are treated as applicable to Sudarshan Colorants India Limited, which forms the current reporting boundary. BRSR disclosures are made on a standalone basis with no external assessment or assurance provider.
- Climate Change & Energy Source Diversification is identified as an opportunity: transitioning to clean fuels and renewable energy can reduce GHG emissions and operating costs over the long term while strengthening business resilience, supporting decarbonization targets and enhancing competitiveness in global markets.
- Product Stewardship & Innovation is identified as an opportunity: developing sustainable and bio-based alternatives can reduce the environmental footprint of products while supporting evolving customer demand and regulatory expectations.
- Occupational Health & Safety is managed through periodic training, safety audits, risk assessments, preventive controls and promotion of a strong safety culture across operations.
- Employee Development & Engagement is identified as an opportunity to strengthen employer branding and the Employee Value Proposition through skills, workplace culture and talent attraction and retention.
- Business Ethics & Compliance is addressed through periodic surveys, mandatory training programmes, stronger governance frameworks and adherence to anti-trust and regulatory requirements.
- Grievance redressal mechanisms are in place for every stakeholder group - complaint registers at the main entry gate across sites for communities plus a grievance.redressal@sudarshan.com email for communities, employees, workers and customers; shares@sudarshan.com for shareholders; and published investor contact details.
- CSR is applicable to the Company under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013.
- Diversity: women are 11% of total employees and 5% of total workers (permanent workers 1%), and 33% of the Board of Directors, with no female representation among Key Management Personnel.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Under the head 'Capacity Expansion', the Directors' Report states that during the year the Company continued its expansion plans and incurred capex spend of Rs 25.34 Crore; no individual project cost or commissioning schedule is disclosed. The larger expansion story is footprint optimisation within the group: the Company took deliberate steps to optimize the manufacturing footprint across the Group, with select AZO products being transitioned from Frankfurt to Roha, while Cuddalore is building a combination of commodity and specialty products for the broader industrial market. Entering FY2027 the stated operating priority is a broader product portfolio, disciplined cost reduction and improved capacity utilization across the existing facilities at Navi Mumbai, Roha, Cuddalore and Nagda, rather than greenfield addition. Efforts to localize the premium HP Azo range are taking shape and are expected to unlock new export opportunities from FY2027 onward. Footprint also expanded indirectly through the group: Sudarshan Europe B.V. completed the acquisition of the Heubach Group on March 3, 2025, bringing 58 subsidiaries (including step-down subsidiaries) and two joint venture companies into the Sudarshan Chemical Group, giving the Company access to a ONE Sudarshan platform of 19 manufacturing facilities across 11 countries, 3,825 employees and 4,000+ global customers, plus technical centres and application expertise. On the energy side, a solar installation at Roha now meets approximately 50% of that facility's electricity demand and a hybrid wind-solar model at Cuddalore lifted renewable electricity share from approximately 62% to 75%.

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).
